newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures firm again late, most end up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures firm again late, most end up.

text.p: U.S. debt futures edged up again in late pit trading, with most units posting small gains on the day.

Afternoon turnover stayed light, however, after futures showed little response to testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan that traders said revealed no new insights into the Fed's view of the current economy.

Greenspan told the Senate finance committee Congress should allot more money to improve the consumer price index but should not dictate the means for making adjustments. He also said the Fed considers the CPI upward bias in setting policy.
"He hasn't said anything," said a Eurodollar floor broker before midday of the Greenspan testimony.

Futures reverted to range-trading for the balance of the session, having touched the day's peak during the morning after the American Production and Inventory Control Society (APIC) January business outlook survey fell to 45.9 from 51.8 in December.

March Treasury bond futures backed off, however, after proving unable to muster enough buying interest to plough too far into resistance strewn thickly above 110-20/32. The day's high remained at 110-24/32.
March Treasury bond futures had edged up early after weekly U.S. jobless claims rose 10,000 to 351,000 from a revised 341,000 prior week.
Traders had expected claims to fall 7,000 to 348,000 from the original prior week's 355,000 level.
They turned attention to Friday's advance fourth-quarter U.S. real gross domestic product.
GDP is expected to show a 3.9-percent growth rate and a 2.2-percent increase in the price index. The implicit deflator is forecast rising at a 1.8-percent rate.
The January Chicago purchasing managers' index is seen sticking at 57.4, and December U.S. new home sales are expected to fall to a 745,000-unit annual rate.

March T-bonds ended up 10/32 at 110-18/32, 10-year notes rose 5/32 to 108-07/32, muni-bonds added 8/32 to 114-12/32, March T-bills ended flat at 94.92, and June eurodollars rose two bps to 94.23. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
